title: Outlook for Mac: conversational email drafting, editing and formatting with Copilot (Worldwide)
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly calls the content-analysis setting the only documented device-level control, although Microsoft also documents a broader connected-experiences control. The admin UI reference does not document the named setting, and the claim that Copilot's data reach does not change is not established by the roadmap.

claims.fix: Change controls[0].ui.docs and the corresponding table link to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/privacy/mac-privacy-preferences, which documents the named Cloud Policy setting. Keep the Cloud Policy overview in sources for the navigation portion of the route.

claims.claim: Set the Boolean OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference key in preference domain com.microsoft.office to FALSE to disable content-analysis connected experiences.
claims.quote:
Preference Domain: com.microsoft.office
Key: OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference
Data Type: Boolean
Possible values: TRUE (enabled) FALSE (disabled)
If you set this preference to FALSE, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in certain apps.

claims.claim: The named content-analysis policy is available through Cloud Policy as an alternative to the Mac preference.
claims.quote:
You can also use Cloud Policy and these five policy settings:
Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content
For more information on using Cloud Policy, see Overview of Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Users with a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 subscription signed in with a work or school account cannot turn off content-analysis connected experiences themselves.
claims.quote: If the user has a Microsoft 365 (or Office 365) subscription and is signed in with a work or school account, or if the user has Office LTSC Standard for Mac 2024, then the user can't turn off connected experiences that analyze content.
